transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-07-08 16:00 UTC. Duration: 48 minutes. Attendees listed above.

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for product search relevance. Show of Redwood Console embeddings explorer and Optimize suggestions. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, caching, and data retention. Agreed next steps to run small pilot benchmark.

Topics: hosted embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint, Console demo, Optimize suggestions, security & data residency, pilot scope, success criteria.

[00:00] Maya Chen (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the Platform team at Redwood.

[00:20] Aisha Khan (Customer): Hi, Aisha here, Head of Search at Northbridge Commerce. We run product search and recommendation, trying to improve relevance for long tail queries.

[00:30] Trevor Mills (Customer): Trevor, eng manager, I'll own infra questions.

[00:35] Leila Park (Customer): Leila, data science, we'll run the evaluation.

[00:40] Diego Alvarez (SE): Diego, solutions engineer, I'll walk through the demo — embeddings, rerank flow, and a quick Console tour.

[00:48] Maya: Great — goal for today is a focused hosted API showcase: embeddings + rerank for search relevance, show how Console + Optimize surfaces batching/quant configs, then agree next steps for pilot. Sound good?

[01:05] Aisha: Yep, please — our primary concerns are latency for search, cost per query, and data retention / compliance.

[01:15] Diego: Cool. Very high-level: our hosted embeddings endpoint returns fixed-size vectors; we support multiple model variants in the catalog. Rerank endpoint accepts a candidate set and uses a reranker model to rescore by relevance — you can call it directly or via the hosted search endpoint pattern.

[01:40] Diego: I'll share my screen — oh, slight lag. Mmhmm. Okay opening the Redwood Console — top nav shows Models, Endpoints, Optimize.

[02:05] [Screen share noise / clicking]

[02:12] Diego: Under Models, you can pick the embeddings model — we expose performance metrics: median latency, 95th, token units per call, cost estimate. For example, our 'emb-medium-v2' has ~15ms median per vector and recommended for short product titles.

[02:35] Leila: Wait — 15ms per vector, is that at 1k concurrency or single request?

[02:40] Diego: That's at our hosted baseline — single request p95 measured on our regions; actual latency depends on payload size and batching. For bulk indexing we suggest the batch CSV upload or the bulk embeddings endpoint which can process thousands with amortized cost.

[02:55] Trevor: What about number of dims? 512 or 1024? That affects index size and vector DB cost.

[03:05] Diego: Typically 768 for the model we demo. You can choose models with 512/1024 depending on your quality needs. Optimize tab will recommend dimension / quantization tradeoffs.

[03:25] [00:03:25 — small pause, typing sounds]

[03:30] Diego: Switching to a live demo: we have a mini product catalog — 2,000 docs. I'll call the embeddings endpoint to index a sample doc and then run a rerank flow for query 'waterproof hiking boots size 11'.

[03:50] [HTTP request noise, command-line pasted]

[04:00] Diego: Here's a cURL example — POST to api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings with api_key header. Request body shows the texts array. Response returns 'vector' field. Note in the Console we also provide an embeddings explorer to preview vectors and cosine distances.

[04:25] Leila: Are vectors stored by Redwood or do we push to our own DB?

[04:32] Diego: On hosted mode we store vectors transiently if you use our managed vector store; but we also support an ephemeral mode where you can fetch vectors and push to your own Pinecone/Weaviate/OpenSearch cluster. If you use managed store, retention policies are configurable — default retention is 30 days for hosted evaluations, but enterprise customers can set longer retention or disable persistent storage.

[04:58] Aisha: Important — we can't have PII retained. We need KMS key control and audit logs.

[05:05] Rina Patel (SE): Absolutely — we have KMS integrations for Private + Dedicated customers; for hosted we offer an encryption-at-rest and a managed KMS option. We'll share the security brief that lists SOC 2, TLS, KMS, and audit log capabilities.

[05:20] Maya: We'll attach the security doc and the SAMPLE SOC2 report.

[05:30] Diego: Back to rerank: flow is usually — embed the query, retrieve a candidate set from your vector DB (we demo with our doc store), then post candidates to /v1/rerank with query + candidate text + metadata. The reranker returns scores and we show ordering confidence.

[05:55] [06:00] Diego: I'll run a rerank call now. You can see the JSON payload — query, candidates array, each with id, title, snippet. Response shows top-5 with scores.

[06:20] Leila: The scores — how calibrated are they? Do they map to probability or relative rank?

[06:25] Diego: They are model scores — monotonically increasing with relevance, not strict probabilities. We surface a normalized score in Console to help thresholds. You can calibrate with your labeled data using our eval harness.

[06:40] Leila: Nice. Does Redwood provide A/B rollout to test reranker in production?

[06:48] Samir Rao (Product): Yes — Console supports rollout policies: canary %, user segments, and automatic fallback to a baseline model if latency spikes or errors increase. That ties into our tracing and cost dashboards.

[07:05] Trevor: Latency SLOs — what are realistic numbers for a rerank of top-50 candidates?

[07:12] Diego: For a hosted reranker, scoring 50 candidates tends to be in the 40–120ms range depending on model size. We also support continuous batching which can lower per-candidate cost if you run many rerank requests in parallel.

[07:30] Aisha: Hmm — our SLA requirement is <120ms 95th for search. Any guarantee?

[07:35] Maya: For hosted we provide documented p95 baselines; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency tiers. For strict 95th <120ms we'd recommend a Dedicated pool or pin to a smaller reranker model plus prefix caching. We can model expected latency for your query footprint during the pilot.

[07:55] [Background cross-talk: someone logging into VPN?]

[08:05] Diego: Speaking of caching — Redwood supports prefix and KV caching on the serving side. For product search, caching top intents or heavy queries reduces upstream cost. Optimize will suggest cache TTLs based on your traffic patterns.

[08:25] Leila: How do pricing units look for rerank vs embeddings?

[08:30] Maya: Embeddings billed per vector unit; reranker billed per call and token usage. We'll send a worked example for your mix (we estimated 1.2M queries / mo in the RFP).

[08:45] Trevor: If we do hosted + managed vector store, what's egress / storage policy? Data residency — we need EU region for our EU customers.

[08:55] Diego: Hosted endpoints are region-aware; you can pin to eu-west-1 or us-east-1. Managed vector store replication options include single-region and cross-region. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.

[09:15] Jonah Reed (Infra): Any network requirements? We prefer SAML SSO and scoping to certain IPs.

[09:20] Rina: We're SAML-friendly across Console access; for API use we support API keys and mTLS for Dedicated/Private. IP allowlist is available.

[09:35] Aisha: Great. Can you show Optimize suggestions now?

[09:40] Diego: Sure — Optimize tab shows workload analysis: token distribution, median sequence length, suggested batching and quantization. For our sample corpus Optimize recommends embeddings quantization to int8 for cost reduction with 2% quality delta.

[09:58] Leila: Is there an automated quantization job or do we have to convert models ourselves?

[10:02] Diego: On Redwood Optimize we propose a quantization profile and can apply it on the serving side for compatible models — no customer-side model conversion required. We can run a safety check and A/B to validate quality.

[10:18] [10:18 — brief pause while Diego pulls up graphs]

[10:25] Diego: Now a quick end-to-end demo: query -> embeddings retrieval -> rerank -> Console logs. You can see per-route token cost in the console and a waterfall trace showing where time is spent: network, model, and post-processing.

[10:47] Trevor: Those traces — can we forward them into our Datadog / Sumo?

[10:52] Samir: Yes — we have tracing hooks and exports. We can push per-request traces or aggregated metrics.

[11:00] Aisha: We're also concerned about cold-starts during peak sale events. How does Redwood handle bursts?

[11:06] Diego: Hosted supports autoscaling with warm pools; Dedicated supports reserved capacity with burst policies. For flash sales we recommend a hybrid approach: Dedicated baseline + hosted overflow.

[11:20] Leila: For evaluation, we want to run our queries and see precision@5 and NDCG improvements. Does Redwood provide an eval harness?

[11:28] Diego: Yes — our eval harness accepts labeled queries and ground truth, runs comparisons across model variants (embedding dims, reranker models), and produces metrics and charts. We'll run that during the pilot using your query set.

[11:45] Aisha: Perfect. What's the onboarding timeline? We're aiming to ship a relevance improvement in Q3 (by end of September).

[11:53] Maya: Pilot timeline typical: week 0 — kickoff and data exchange; week 1 — benchmark run; week 2 — tuning and A/B; week 3 — roll to a small percentage in production. So Q3 is achievable.

[12:10] Trevor: Any blockers for us to start the pilot? We need NDA? Procurement?

[12:15] Maya: We'll send an MSA and a pilot addendum. Procurement usually takes 2–3 weeks for enterprise customers; pilot can start under a trial agreement if the security team approves.

[12:28] [12:28 — quick side note: someone drops a link in chat]

[12:35] Diego: I want to highlight one more thing: the rerank endpoint supports per-candidate metadata passthrough so you can include price, inventory flags, or recency; the model can be constrained via features so rerank isn't purely semantic — you can apply business rules post-score.

[12:55] Leila: That's helpful — we need recency to bias new arrivals.

[13:00] Diego: We demo a small snippet in the notebook — show how to include a recency boost in post-processing.

[13:15] [13:15 — typing]

[13:22] Diego: Last piece: cost optimization — Optimize suggests batching index jobs, using smaller embedding dims for facets, and quantized models for bulk rerank. It will also estimate savings and expected quality delta.

[13:40] Aisha: Any case studies for retail customers?

[13:45] Maya: Yes, we'll attach a short retail case study — search relevance uplift and cost numbers.

[13:52] Trevor: Ok, let's recap next steps.

[13:55] Maya: Recap: Redwood sends pricing + security docs; Diego shares rerank notebook + cURL examples; Northbridge provides anonymized query logs and sample corpus; schedule pilot kickoff early next week pending procurement.

[14:12] Aisha: Agreed. Also can you include a short checklist for compliance folks?

[14:18] Maya: Yes — we'll include a compliance checklist + regional hosting options.

[14:25] Jonah: I'll coordinate with Trevor on VPC/network items.

[14:28] Trevor: Great. Any final questions?

[14:32] Leila: One small one — how do we measure model regressions over time?

[14:36] Diego: We have quality monitoring — you can send prompt sets and ground-truth labels as part of continuous eval. The Console raises regression alerts and can block rollouts if metric drops exceed thresholds.

[14:50] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[14:55] Aisha: Thanks — good session.

[15:00] [Recording ends]

Notes: Minor transcription artifacts: 'K V cash' appears once in transcript instead of KV cache. Some proper nouns may be mis-capitalized.
